Contracts sqlite

One schema folder, four entities, each picking which contracts it generates

Match — entlite.SQLC() and entlite.PROTO() A match table in sqlite and a MatchService in proto

Player — entlite.SQLC() and entlite.PROTO().ReadOnly() A player table keyed by name and a PlayerService with read rpc only, seeded by the server

Standing — entlite.PROTO() only No table, the handler counts the standings from matches on every call

Audit — entlite.SQLC() only Written on every match create and delete, no proto message, no rpc

What's happening:
Every entity declares its own Contracts(). Match declares both, so it gets a table in ent/contract/sqlc and a service in ent/contract/proto. Player declares both too, but its proto contract is ReadOnly(), so the table and the queries are there while the service has only GetByName and ListAll — the server seeds the roster with the generated CreatePlayer query, which never became an rpc. Standing declares only entlite.PROTO(), so it is a message and a service with no table behind it — the rank arrives in its id field. Audit declares only entlite.SQLC(), so it has a table and generated queries but no proto message, no ToProto() and no rpc, which is why its count comes from a plain HTTP endpoint instead.
